newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close higher, BOK forecasts ignored.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close higher, BOK forecasts ignored.

text.p: South Korean stocks closed higher on Friday after investors ignored the central bank's downward revision of its forecast for this year's economic growth.
The composite index ended 8.68 points higher at 687.42.

Shipbuilding firms rose to their daily limits on news that shipbuilding orders for the first quarter of this year increased 166.7 percent from a year earlier. Petrochemical shares climbed as investors thought these companies would benefit from a fire and the resulting suspention of a polyethylene plant in Japan.
The market will be closed on Saturday for Arbour Day.
"The central bank's revision made no impact when most investors believed the economy had bottomed out," said Shim Choong-bo, research manager at Daishin Securities.

The Bank of Korea on Friday revised its forecast for this year's gross domestic product growth to 5.5-6.0 percent from 6.4 percent. It also said this year's current account deficit could exceed its earlier forecast of $18 billion.

All the three listed shipbuilders rose to their daily limits. Dewoo Heavy Industries was up 350 won to 4,800, Hanjin Heavy Industries up 550 won to 7,520 and Samsung Heavy Industries up 590 won to 7,990.
Polyethylene makers rose on the news that a polyethylene plant in Japan, owned jointly by DuPont Co and Mitsui Petrochemical Industries Ltd, was shut after a fire broke out.
LG Chemical was up 600 won to 10,900, Daelim Industrial up 440 won to 8,500 and Hanwha Chemical up 650 won to 8,950.
